units.title: 1 Religions, traditions and practices before the prophethood of Muhammad (pbuh)

outcomes.text: Describe tribal and political organisation, including the Bedouin and the Quraysh.
Explain social conditions and the economy: Makkah trade, pilgrim trade, slavery and infanticide.
Outline the religious groups present, polytheist and monotheist, with their beliefs and practices.
Identify the hanifs who followed Ibrahim's religion in Muhammad's early life.
Explain why the Kaʿba in Makkah was central to pilgrimage and worship.
Tell Adam's story: creation, the Garden, coming to Earth, and life with his family.
Tell how Musa grew up in Pharaoh's household and what got him into trouble.
Describe Musa's prophethood, the confrontation and miracles before Pharaoh, and the escape from Egypt.
Tell how Yusuf's brothers' jealousy separated him from his family and brought him to Egypt.
Describe the Zulaikhah episode, Yusuf's imprisonment and release, and the family reunion.
Tell of ʿIsa's virgin birth, his speech as an infant, his time in the Temple, and his ministry and miracles.
Describe Ibrahim rejecting idols, searching for truth, and surviving the fire.
Recount Ibrahim's talk with the king and God's test of sacrificing his son Ismaʿil.
Narrate Muhammad's life from birth to the call to prophethood and the first revelation in Cave Hiraʾ.
Describe the Prophet's early preaching, the opposition, persecution of Muslims, and the hijrah to Madinah.
Explain the problems the Prophet faced in Makkah and the reasons for opposition to his message.
Explain how he handled relatives and opponents, including the exile in the valley and escape from Taʾif.
Explain the Constitution of Madinah, relations with other religious groups, and the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah.
Describe the Prophet's successes and achievements in Madinah.

subtopics.title: Battles of Badr, Uhud and Trench

outcomes.text: Give causes, events and consequences of the battles of Badr, Uhud and the Trench.
Describe the conquest of Makkah, the farewell address and farewell Hajj, and their message for relations with other groups.

topics.title: 2.3 From the whole of the Prophet’s life

outcomes.text: Show the Prophet's patience and forgiveness with opponents and how he built community strength.
Describe his relationship with and care for his wives and daughters.

units.title: 3 Texts from the Holy Qurʾan and Hadith

outcomes.text: Explain Surah 63:9-11, on charity and accountability to God, with the context of revelation.
Explain Surah 94, God's consolation in worry and difficulty, with its context.
Explain Surah 95, on belief and righteous deeds in God's judgement, with its context.
Explain Surah 103, on faith, deeds, rightful teaching and patience, with its context.
Explain Surah 107, on being genuine rather than superficial, with its context.
Explain Surah 110, on God's help and support, with its context.
Explain Surah 113, on guarding against mischief-making and envy, with its context.
Explain Hadith 5, rejection of innovation, and its context.
Explain Hadith 9, about obedience, and its context.
Explain Hadith 12, not interfering with others, and its context.
Explain Hadith 20, about having shame, and its context.
Explain Hadith 30, about neglecting religious obligations, and its context.
Explain Hadith 31, about not being attached to worldly possessions, and its context.
Explain Hadith 32, not causing or responding to harm, and its context.
Describe how Abu Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿUthman and ʿAli accepted Islam and responded to the Prophet's message.
Explain how each Caliph was elected, the role of consultation, and the circumstances of each.
Illustrate the Caliphs' piety, humility, bravery, strength and kindness with examples.
Show how the Caliphs followed the Prophet's sunnah.
Explain how each Caliph organised and administered the caliphate.
Describe the social and religious facilities the Caliphs provided for people.
Describe how the Caliphs responded to difficulties.
Discuss the Caliphs, their characters and families as examples and inspiration for Muslims today.

units.title: 5 The Qurʾan, Hadith and Muslim beliefs and practices

outcomes.text: Explain the Qurʾan's status as God's revealed word and the basis of all thought and action.
Describe how revelation came to the Prophet, beginning with Laylat al-Qadr.
Explain the Qurʾan's transmission, collection, preservation and compilation, including Zayd ibn Thabit's role.
Describe how the Qurʾan is used in Muslims' lives and worship.
Explain the Hadith as the Prophet's teachings, deeds and sayings.
Describe how Hadith was collected, tested for authenticity, and classed as sahih, hasan, daʿif or mawduʿ.
Explain the meaning of the Hadith and its significance for Muslims today.

topics.title: 5.2 Articles of Faith and the Five Pillars of Islam

outcomes.text: Give an overview of the Articles of Faith and their basis in the Qurʾan and sunnah.
Study in detail the oneness of God (tawhid).
Study in detail prophethood (risalah).
Study in detail beliefs about the afterlife (akhirah).
Explain the statement of faith (shahadah): observance, significance and benefits.
Explain daily prayer (salah): observance, significance and benefits.
Explain alms tax (zakah): observance, significance and benefits.
Explain fasting (sawm) in Ramadan: observance, significance and benefits.
Explain pilgrimage (Hajj) to Makkah: observance, significance and benefits.

units.title: 6 Festivals, rituals and social interactions in the lives of Muslims

outcomes.text: Describe ʿId al-Fitr: moon sighting, sunnah and traditions, ʿId prayer, social customs and charity.
Describe ʿId al-Adha: its link to Hajj events, the ʿId prayer, the ummah and fresh commitment.
Explain the aqiqah, family life, and teaching a child about Islam.
Explain choosing partners, the nikah, and the importance of family life.
Describe beliefs about death, burial preparation, the funeral prayer (janazah), and mourning traditions.

topics.title: 6.3 Social interactions in the lives of Muslims

outcomes.text: Explain the importance of family, caring for the elderly and respecting parents.
Describe how Muslims support mosques and those in need and build good relations with those of other views.
Explain environmental responsibility, traditions about crops and trees, and Muslim responses to environmental issues.
